name: Pick
text: I think we should start by monitoring Reddit's r/MachineLearning and r/AI communities, as they have a massive following and a constant flow of new information. This decision makes sense because these communities are known for discussing the latest advancements and breakthroughs in AI, which aligns with our goal of gathering diverse AI info. By focusing on these communities, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially missing out on some niche or specialized information that might be available on other platforms. I believe this is a good compromise, as the sheer volume and quality of information on Reddit will give us a solid foundation to build upon.

name: Assay
text: While monitoring Reddit's r/MachineLearning and r/AI communities may seem appealing due to their popularity, there's a significant risk of encountering unverified or exaggerated claims that could lead us astray. A better alternative might be to focus on reputable sources like academic journals or established AI publications, which provide more reliable information. To settle this argument, we could outline a criteria list to assess the credibility of the sources we consider, ensuring we prioritize quality over quantity.
